title: Companion faithfulness findings, schema v2
description: One findings file per task. v1 (the 2,672-file baseline) differed in four ways: no schema_version/run_id/source_sha, `faithful` was a single string, the witness lived in `reasoning` prose, and there was no finding_id. v1 also predates the multi-source model: it had one implicit book, so its `book_sha` slot becomes `source_sha` and scripts/gate/convert_v1.py stamps the run's single `source_id` on the document and on every disagreement (--source is required). `book_quote`/`book_passage_quote`/`book_located` deliberately keep their names — they are still quotes from a book; what changed is WHICH text they are verified against, which `source_id` decides. scripts/gate/convert_v1.py maps v1 to this schema without touching the baseline. The gate that enforces this is scripts/gate/verify_findings.py, which is driven by gate.json (kinds, verdicts, repos, witness requirement, per-kind rules) rather than by this file: no jsonschema dependency is assumed anywhere in the skill. `disagreements` is the canonical defect key and stays required; because scripts/harvest/tally.py and scripts/ledger/findings.py also count rows carried under `findings`, the gate validates that key too (DEFECT_LISTS) and refuses any other top-level array of rows carrying a `kind`.

run_id.description: the run that produced this file; part of finding_id

source_id.description: which source this file read: the key in workspace.yaml `sources:`. An item is the pair (source_id, item), so a bare item is never a cross-source key, and the gate picks the text a quote is matched against by this field.

source_sha.description: sha256 of that source's PDF bytes (was `book_sha`), stamped on every artifact that quotes or anchors a source

item.description: book item id, e.g. 'Exercise 1.3.19' or 'In-text, book p. 35'

book_passage_quote.description: verbatim from the book text; machine-verified

verdict.description: the gate takes the permitted set from gate.json; legacy presets also accept NO_WEAKNESS_FOUND, which convert_v1.py folds into NO_DEFECT_FOUND

source_id.description: the source this row is about; inherited from the document when absent

source_sha.description: that source's sha256, inherited from the document when absent

finding_id.description: sha256(run_id, source_id, item, kind, sorted(unfaithful_decls)) — stable across runs of the same defect, unlike v1's LLM-written concept. source_id is a part because `Exercise 1.3.19` of two sources is two different items.

kind.description: PAGE_ANCHOR is mechanical-only (source: anchor_check); no LLM preset lists it

faithful.description: v2: a LIST of repos that got it right; [] when none did. v1's 'none'/'all_differ'/'unsure' survive in faithful_note.

unfaithful_decls.description: 'repo:decl'; routing keys on this prefix and nothing else

witness.description: required on CONTENT/VACUITY in attack mode; presence and non-emptiness are mechanical, judging it is the reviewer's job

d.description: the dimension, when the book's objects are dimensional

source.description: e.g. v1_reasoning_lift for converted baseline rows

closure.description: PROXY findings only: the dependency path that reaches the proxied object
